title: The Last Will Revisited
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Merrick, founder of the coastal town of Tidehaven, is exhumed for a disputed will hearing, it proves empty—and the only person who signed the burial log is Vesper Galloway, a night dispatcher who has spent years making herself unnoticeable. Pulled into the investigation by an old friend on the police force, Vesper follows radio chatter, taxi manifests, and tide charts to uncover that Merrick faked his death to escape blackmail tied to the town's founding fortune, and that the 'dead' witness everyone cites—his former chauffeur, Ruth Okafor—is alive and hiding in plain sight. As Vesper closes in, she must choose between protecting Ruth, who once saved her life, and telling the truth that will save Tidehaven from the Merrick heirs' fraud. In the end, the sea gives up what it took: Merrick's body, drowned the night of his fake funeral, and Vesper testifies, trading her invisibility for a town's reckoning.
about_author: Hazel Halloran spent a decade answering phones at a harbor-town taxi dispatch before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about people who overhear everything and are believed by no one.

chapters.title: The Grave That Wouldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Vesper Galloway, night-shift dispatcher, watches from the courthouse steps as Aldous Merrick's coffin is opened and found empty. Her name is in the burial log as the last witness to sign. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dread—the invisibility she cultivated begins to crack.

chapters.title: Dispatch at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Back at the cab office, Vesper replays the night of Merrick's funeral through old call logs, finding a fare she never logged. Detective Imogen Reyes arrives asking questions. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve; she decides to look before she's accused.

chapters.title: The Heirs Arrive
chapters.summary: Merrick's three heirs descend on Tidehaven for the will contest, each with alibis too polished. Vesper drives one of them and hears a slip about 'the chauffeur problem.' POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: unease—the family knows more than the police do.

chapters.title: A Name No One Says
chapters.summary: Vesper researches Ruth Okafor, Merrick's chauffeur listed as deceased in the probate file, though no death certificate exists. A retired gravedigger hints the funeral was rushed. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: first real hope that the case has a living thread.

chapters.title: Static on Line Two
chapters.summary: A garbled call comes into dispatch asking for 'the girl who signs logs,' then hangs up. Vesper traces the number to a shuttered cannery. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: fear mixed with recognition—a voice she almost remembers.

chapters.title: Imogen's Warning
chapters.summary: Detective Reyes shares that the exhumation was ordered by an anonymous letter, and warns Vesper someone inside the department may be feeding the heirs information. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two women who trust slowly.

chapters.title: The Cannery at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper searches the cannery and finds a cot, canned food, and a woman's coat—recently used. Footsteps above send her fleeing without being seen. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: confirmation tinged with terror; the witness is alive and close.

chapters.title: What the Log Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: years earlier, teenage Vesper survived a crash because a chauffeur pulled her from the water—Ruth Okafor, before she vanished. POV: Vesper (memory). Emotional beat: the debt that binds her loyalty against the truth.

chapters.title: Blackmail and Founding Money
chapters.summary: Digging through archived newspapers, Vesper learns Merrick's fortune began with a drowned partner whose death was ruled accidental. The heirs' lawyer starts following her. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the town's beloved history curdles into something rotten.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Vesper realizes a cab from her own fleet is tailing her—someone at the company is working for the heirs. She feeds the driver false routes. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: paranoia, then cold competence; invisibility becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Another anonymous letter forces the hearing adjourned; Imogen suspects the writer wants time, not justice. Vesper suspects the writer is Ruth herself. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: the investigation splits—police logic versus Vesper's intuition.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Taxi Routes
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing tides with dispatch records, Vesper maps where a body could have entered the water the week after the funeral. One route matches: Gull Point. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grim clarity—the founder may truly be dead after all.

chapters.title: Face to Face
chapters.summary: At the cannery, Vesper finally meets Ruth Okafor, older, guarded, alive. Ruth admits she helped Merrick stage his death—then found him dead anyway, and has been hiding ever since. POV: alternating Vesper/Ruth. Emotional beat: relief colliding with betrayal.

chapters.title: Ruth's Account
chapters.summary: Ruth tells the whole story: the blackmail over the partner's murder, the staged funeral, Merrick's plan to flee by boat, and the morning his boat washed up empty. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: confession as unburdening; loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Someone Followed Her
chapters.summary: Leaving the cannery, Vesper spots the heir's lawyer photographing the door. She leads him on a chase through back roads and loses him—but now the heirs know Ruth lives. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: protective panic; the clock starts running.

chapters.title: Pressure at Dispatch
chapters.summary: The cab company's owner, revealed to be on the heirs' payroll, suspends Vesper and demands her notes. She copies the dispatch archives first. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that made her invisible.

chapters.title: Imogen Crosses the Line
chapters.summary: Imogen confirms the mole is her own sergeant and goes off-book to protect Vesper and Ruth, stashing them at a lighthouse keeper's cottage. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: duty redefined—loyalty to people over procedure.

chapters.title: The Heirs Close In
chapters.summary: The eldest heir offers Vesper money to stay silent, then threatens Ruth's exposure when she refuses. Vesper records the conversation. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into leverage; she stops running.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: After a storm, Merrick's remains surface at Gull Point with evidence of drowning and a struggle—killed by one of his own children the night of the escape. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grief for a man she never knew, and horror at how neatly the town buried it.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Vesper takes the stand, plays the recording, and presents the dispatch archive; Ruth enters under subpoena protection. The will is voided and the heirs are charged. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the climax—invisibility traded, voice finally used.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Cab Office
chapters.summary: Reinstated, Vesper returns to the night shift changed: drivers greet her by name, and Imogen brings coffee. Ruth decides to stay in Tidehaven openly. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: quiet belonging earned rather than hidden into.

chapters.title: The Last Will Revisited
chapters.summary: Months later, Vesper visits Merrick's true grave and leaves a taxi receipt dated the night he died—closing the log she once signed falsely. The tide keeps its own records now. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: resolution—truth settled, loyalty honored, inheritance refused.
